extracted.intended_audience: individuals preparing public comments on pending federal agency regulations (advocates, researchers, practitioners, concerned citizens)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting effective, evidence-backed public comments to federal agencies during rulemaking, emphasizing clarity, credibility, and actionable recommendations that respond to the regulatory prompt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and understand the proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and understand the proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the full proposed rule thoroughly before writing. Understand the text, definitions, and regulatory questions; contact agency staff if clarification is needed. Familiarity with the document ensures substantive, relevant comments rather than superficial reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific questions in the regulatory prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: Address any specific questions in the regulatory prompt
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly respond to the agency's listed questions or requests for comment. Organize portions of your comment to answer those prompts explicitly so reviewers can see how your input maps to the issues the agency asked about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish your credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish your credentials by stating who you are and why the proposed regulation is relevant to you
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the start, state your identity, expertise, organizational affiliation, and personal relevance to the regulation. Explain relevant professional experience and personal investment so reviewers can assess the weight and perspective of your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete suggestions and changes to the proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete suggestions and changes to the proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer specific, actionable alternatives or edits (e.g., suggested regulatory text or precise policy modifications). Support recommendations with data, explain underlying assumptions, and when appropriate present pros/cons or implementation considerations rather than only high-level objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support all claims and arguments with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Support all claims and arguments with evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back assertions with citations, data, studies, economic analyses, or documented real-world impacts (health, safety, costs). Where opposing evidence exists, directly refute it with evidence. Evidence-based comments carry more weight than anecdote or opinion alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the recommended structure (Introduction, Overview, Major Concerns, Conclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended Structure — Introduction: Establish credentials; Overview: Summarize major issues, principal arguments, and specific recommendations; Major Concerns: Detail arguments with supporting evidence (organize by regulatory questions, concerns, or alternative solutions with pros/cons); Conclusion: Re-summarize recommendations (skimmers may read only this section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the comment with clear section headings. Introduction should state who you are and why you comment. The overview gives a concise roadmap. Major Concerns should provide detailed, evidence-backed arguments organized logically (by question, concern, or proposed alternative). End with a short conclusion that reiterates key recommendations—many reviewers skim and may read only the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze and tailor the comment to the agency/audience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the specific agency or official, tailoring tone and content appropriately. Avoid technical jargon or explain technical terms (assume non-scientific reviewers). Focus on real-world impacts (economic effects, health outcomes) the agency cares about. Remember that comments may become public and write accordingly.
